step1_figure.description: An N-stage voltage multiplier that uses diode-connected MOSFETs and clock-driven capacitors to pump charge and generate a high DC voltage. The netlist implements a 6-stage version of this pump.

multiplier_output_swing_high.description: The maximum voltage reached at the last pumped node of the multiplier during steady state.

equation.explanation: The peak voltage at the Nth pumped stage, assuming ideal clock coupling and no DC load.
equation.assumptions: No DC load, ideal clock swing, steady state, ignores body effect.

sky130_expected.calculation: For N=6 pumped stages (nodes N001 to N006): (6+1)*1.8V - 6*0.42V = 12.6V - 2.52V = 10.08V
sky130_expected.reasoning: The theoretical maximum is 10.08V. However, because the bulk of all NMOS devices is tied to ground (0V), the source-to-bulk voltage (Vsb) increases significantly at each stage. This severe body effect increases VTHN well above 0.42V for the later stages, causing the actual maximum voltage to be noticeably lower than the ideal calculation.

multiplier_output_swing_low.description: The minimum voltage reached at the last pumped node of the multiplier during steady state.

equation.explanation: The valley voltage at the Nth pumped stage when its driving clock goes low.
equation.assumptions: No DC load, ideal clock swing, steady state, ignores body effect.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Similar to the high swing, the severe body effect on the diode-connected NMOS transistors will increase the threshold voltage drops across the chain, resulting in a lower actual valley voltage than the ideal 8.28V.

step3_testbench.description: Transient analysis to measure the steady-state pumped voltages and the final DC output of the Dickson charge pump.
